policy_context.execution_authorization_reference: Current explicit owner instruction 2026-10-22 authorizes bounded exploratory M4 measurements and remeasurement after material instrumentation changes, using fresh operation IDs and full containment; no retry after a gate failure and no hard-gate bypass.
policy_context.resource_basis: One bounded paired same-binary comparison of the pre-staging flush query-lock boundary (baseline) versus metadata publication staging (candidate). Each arm seeds the same 8,192 Jieba documents, runs four WAL-durable writers × eight Upserts with two readers during one default compaction, then starts two continuous readers before explicit Flush and keeps them active until at least two post-flush queries each. The verifier requires per-reader timestamps proving at least two completed queries before, one query started during and overlapping the flush interval, and two queries after; a larger query count without interval overlap is invalid. Both modes preserve WAL fsync, manifest-before-publication and reopen/replay semantics. Capture per-query total wall, native query-mutex wait and execution CPU; flush total/stage wall+CPU and query-lock wait/hold; writer p95/state wait; fsync and bytes-written counters; cgroup/host memory, CPU and I/O evidence. Single operation only, no retry if any gate, containment or overlap check fails. Exploratory evidence, not qualification, a stable p95 claim, or production authorization. Concurrent flush remains out of scope.
policy_context.risk_acceptance_reference: The standard contention profile is four-arm; writer_group_commit is a separate two-arm per-call Upsert experiment. All are descriptive only: shared-host pressure, one round per arm and test-scale workloads prohibit causal, qualification or architecture-win claims. ApplyBatch and Upsert call latencies have different units and must not be compared as equivalent tail samples.
